claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits large magnetocaloric effects.
The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits large barocaloric effects.
The untreated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack under mechanical stress.
Localized pulsed laser remelting will increase the alloy's load-bearing integrity.
Localized pulsed laser remelting will preserve the alloy's bulk caloric response under magnetic fields.
Localized pulsed laser remelting will preserve the alloy's bulk caloric response under pressure fields.
A laser energy density on the order of several J/cm² can remelt and rapidly resolidify only the top approximately 50–100 μm of the alloy.
Rapid laser melting and resolidification will produce a nanocrystalline surface layer.
The remelted surface layer will have a reduced residual-defect density.
The remelted surface layer will have improved toughness.
A dense nanocrystalline surface layer will resist surface crack initiation.
A dense nanocrystalline surface layer will resist crack propagation.
Confining treatment to a shallow surface layer will leave the bulk microstructure responsible for reversible caloric phase transitions intact.
The treatment will increase crack-initiation load and fatigue life relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy's field-induced entropy change will remain equivalent to that of the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy's caloric reversibility will remain equivalent to that of the untreated alloy.
The intervention is applicable during magnetocaloric and barocaloric operation at 280–320 K under moderate pressures and tensile or bending loads.
